candidates.exact_span: Pollutant Table (2 or 3) appropriate for permittee's land app lication practices.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which pollutant table applies depends on how land application practices are interpreted; Table 2 and Table 3 carry different numeric limits and reporting frameworks, so a different table selection changes applicable discharge limits and which monitoring/reporting requirements govern the permittee.

candidates.exact_span: The frequency of monitoring listed in Element 1, Section I.C. which applies to the permittee.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Monitoring obligation applicability hinges on which Element 1, Section I.C. frequency provision applies to the permittee; a different interpretation of that cross-reference changes whether monitoring was required.

TCLP is evaluated on a Pass/Fail basis rather than a numeric concentration; interpreting this as enforceable numeric limit comparison versus categorical report-only monitoring changes limit-exceedance analysis (A), whether TCLP sampling was required (B), and how missing or non-numeric TCLP results are classified (C).

candidates.exact_span: The concentration (mg/Kg) in the sludge of each pollutant listed in Table 1 (defined as a monthly average) as well as the applicable pollutant concentration criteria (mg/K g) listed in Table 3 found in Element 1, Section III, or the applicable pollutant loading rate limit (kg/ha) listed in Table 2 above if it exceeds 90% of the limit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage ties reported concentrations to multiple possible limit types (Table 3 concentration criteria vs Table 2 loading rate limits), defines them as monthly averages, and conditions Table 2 limit reporting on a 90% threshold; different readings of which limit applies, how monthly averaging is performed, or whether the 90% trigger is met would change limit comparisons (A), reporting/monitoring obligations (B), and how borderline or missing results are handled (C).

candidates.exact_span: Level of pathogen reduction achieved (Class A or Class B).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether sludge is Class A or Class B determines which pathogen-related monitoring and supplemental reporting obligations apply; misclassification changes evaluated monitoring requirements (B) and how missing pathogen-reduction evidence is interpreted (C).

candidates.exact_span: Alternative used as listed in Section I.B.3.(a. or b.). Alternatives describe how the pathogen reduction requirements are met. If Class B sludge, include information on how site restrictions were met in the DMR comment section or attach a separate sheet to the DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which Section I.B.3 alternative is used and whether Class B site-restriction documentation was required depend on permittee-specific pathogen-reduction status; different interpretations change conditional monitoring/reporting obligations (B) and whether absent site-restriction information reflects a documented no-data state or unresolved required evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: The certification statement listed in 503.17(a)(4)(i)(B) or 503.17(a)(5)(i)(B) whichever applies to the permittees sludge treatment activities shall be attached to the DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Applicability turns on which 503.17 certification subsection matches the permittee's sludge treatment activities; choosing the wrong subsection changes which documentation was required (B) and whether missing certification reflects unresolved evidence versus a non-applicable requirement (C).

candidates.exact_span: When the amount of any pollutant applied to the land exceeds 90% of the cumulative pollutant loading rate for that pollutant, as described in Table 2, the permittee shall report the following information as an attachment to the DMR.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 90% threshold against Table 2 cumulative pollutant loading rates triggers additional attachment reporting; interpreting cumulative applied amounts or the threshold differently changes proximity-to-limit analysis (A), whether supplemental reporting was required (B), and what evidence must exist when results are near limits or absent (C).

candidates.exact_span: The cumulative amount of each pollutant (i.e., kilograms/hectare) listed in Table 2 in the bulk sewage sludge applied to each site.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Site-level cumulative pollutant loading must be compared against Table 2 limits to determine both compliance status and whether the 90% reporting trigger is met; different interpretations of cumulative kilograms/hectare per site change limit-exceedance results (A) and conditional reporting obligations (B).

candidates.exact_span: A description of how the requirements to obtain information in 40 CFR 503.12(e)(2) are met.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This documentation is required only when the 90% cumulative loading trigger applies; whether 503.12(e)(2) information-gathering was required and whether its absence represents a documented no-data state or missing required evidence depends on interpretation of that conditional trigger (B, C).

candidates.exact_span: For those permittees with sludge that contains concentrations of pollutants below those pollutant limits listed in Table 3 for bulk or bagged (containerized) sewage sludge and also meet the Class A pathogen reduction requirements, the following conditions apply
candidates.computation_change_reason: Section III applicability is conditional on pollutant concentrations being below Table 3 limits and achieving Class A pathogen reduction; different readings of whether those prerequisites are met change which enforceable Table 3 limits and associated conditions govern the permittee (A) and which requirement set is evaluated (B).

candidates.exact_span: All bagged sewage sludge must be treated by Class A pathogen reduction requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether sludge is bagged determines a mandatory Class A pathogen-reduction obligation; interpreting bulk-versus-bagged status differently changes which pathogen-related monitoring requirements were applicable (B).
